title: Limit Theory for Isotonic-Propensity ATT Estimation on Propensity Plateaus
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: tier=subfield < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 7 < 7.4. Not salvageable within scope; math panel PASS, all citations verified, graph closed.
gap_reasons: The delivered contribution concerns the observed-scalar equation (8) ATT statistic; estimated-index matching and constrained-model efficiency remain outside its proved scope.

The local sampling and bootstrap laws are uniform over admissible directions at a fixed baseline, not over changing plateau geometries, although the interval coverage guarantee covers the full maintained class.

The absolute-imbalance allowance establishes conservative coverage through triangle-inequality domination, without an interval-length optimality result or a comparison establishing its practical precision.

Wald undercoverage is established for sufficiently large finite noise amplitudes, but the package supplies neither a concrete numerical coverage deficit nor reproducible coverage-and-length comparisons for the proposed replacement.
proof_attempt_summary: Derived and reviewed the observed-scalar isotonic ATT plateau/local-bootstrap laws, exact disappearance criterion, continuous Wald-undercoverage family, and data-only honest centered interval with coverage at least 0.90-C n^(-19/125). Source-access, measurability, minorant-path, and bootstrap-interface defects were repaired; the final math panel passed, all eleven citation checks cleared, and the 85-commit graph closed. The final package remained subfield below the field floor because of scope and practical-precision limits, so it was banked before Lean formalization; no F stages or Lean verification were claimed.
tldr: On positive-length propensity plateaus, the original Liu--Qin equation (8) ATT statistic has a joint local limit consisting of the ordinary causal score and a dependent convex-minorant contribution. The latter vanishes exactly when the control mean is constant on every plateau. A data-only interval centered on that statistic has coverage at least \(0.90-Cn^{-19/125}\), uniformly over the maintained monotone-propensity class with fixed overlap, bounded positive measurable design density, a uniform \(C^2\) mean ball, and conditional fourth moments. Its radius combines the observed PAVA imbalance, the estimated ordinary-score standard deviation, and slack \(n^{-1/25}\); it estimates no plateau endpoints and permits zero score variance. The conditional pairs-bootstrap law and a continuous bounded-outcome family establish a failure boundary for the observed-scalar bootstrap-variance Wald workflow. Estimated-index implementations, including direct NSW Table 3 reanalysis, require a separate extension.
gap: Liu--Qin final equation (8) uses ordinary PAVA odds, while its scalar Theorem 3 states a score-only approximation without explicitly excluding plateaus. Its recovered supplement uses an inverse propensity in Lemma 3.5 and bounded fitted probabilities in Section 3.3. Those steps do not establish the requested plateau transfer. Xu--Otsu assumes continuous design density; Armstrong--Kolesar supplies a Lipschitz smoothness example; Liu--Qin assumes finite unconditional second moments. These sources do not establish the maintained measurable-density, uniform \(C^2\), and uniform conditional fourth-moment hypotheses as a published ATT inference package. Section 2.5 and Algorithm 1 (published page 8) prescribe nonparametric pairs-bootstrap variance estimation for the ATT; Table 3 and Section 4 (published page 12) use bootstrap-variance Wald intervals and apply Algorithm 1 to all compared estimators. The published Theorem 5 inherits the stronger hypotheses of Theorem 4 and does not establish this workflow across the declared scalar plateau class.
fill: Integrated convex-minorant methods are adapted to the shared Bernoulli treatment primitive, score covariance, ratio normalization, and control-only suffix convention. The uniform \(C^2\) mean bound controls first-derivative bias of the boundary local polynomial fit, enabling the same-sample \(C^1\) balance-transfer gate. The conditional fourth-moment bound supplies a common conditional residual second-moment envelope and truncation-tail and score-variance control. Quantified transfer and calibration slack remain proof obligations on this maintained class; a Lipschitz version with slower calibration and a weaker-moment version remain open. The continuous family retains the conditional bootstrap law, its second-moment limit, and an actual coverage expansion for the named Algorithm 1 workflow; the negative result is its scalar plateau failure boundary. Theorem 5 of Liu--Qin remains outside that negative comparison under its own stronger hypotheses.
